title: Custom HTML Elements in LLM Chat Responses
summary: ChatGPT embeds structured UI components (product carousels, quick replies) inside Markdown chat responses by using custom Unicode delimiters (U+E200, U+E201, U+E202) within Server-Sent Events streams. The same pattern is buildable with Phoenix LiveView, MDEx, and Web Components: instruct the model in the API prompt about available custom element syntax (e.g. <quick-reply>), configure MDEx with sanitize options that add the custom tag to the allow-list, define an HTMLElement Web Component that handles clicks and submits the chat form, and render the markdown body with MDEx.to_html! piped through raw. LLMs consistently use custom HTML elements when given clear syntax instructions, enabling rich responses like carousels, comparison tables, and expandable sections.

chunks.content: ChatGPT uses custom Unicode delimiters (`U+E200`, `U+E201`, `U+E202`) to embed structured UI components (e.g. product carousels) inside Markdown responses. The same approach can be built with Phoenix LiveView, MDEx, and Web Components.

## How ChatGPT Does It

Responses arrive as Server-Sent Events. A carousel is JSON delimited by special Unicode characters that serve as custom syntax markers. The LLM emits these markers inline with normal Markdown text.

## Key Insight

LLMs are competent at consistently using custom HTML elements when provided with clear syntax instructions. The approach works for more complex elements too — carousels, comparison tables, expandable sections. Equip the model with a menu of custom elements and let it choose the most expressive one for each response.
